speaker: agnes_tipping
text: Pork, if you are staying. The ordinary is on the board.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Pork. I am staying.

speaker: hired_men
text: Ralph Raye. I brought the Rose with the dinner, because you will ask before the plates are down.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Say the money first. I can hear a sum. I have no use for a rumour with no sum in it.

speaker: hired_men
text: Henslowe paid his carpenters seven pounds and two shillings for making a throne in the heavens. A chair. It comes down out of the roof with a god in it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: A chair on a rope, and a yard pays to see a man sit down in the air.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A glass. Four shillings. And it comes down by itself.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Four shillings is a glass. Seven pounds and two shillings is timber and a man's week. Do not put them in the same mouth as if they were the same thing.

speaker: hired_men
text: And yesterday a new play. The Seven Days of the Week. Three pounds ten. The whole Bankside is running to it.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Three pounds ten for a week of days. I hope their Tuesday is shorter than a Tuesday.

speaker: will_kemp
text: If they are running, they are running at a new title. New is a weather of its own. It passes.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: We are not on the Bankside. Let them run. Tell me what the chair does when the rope sticks.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Give me the crust. I will show you, and I will not spend five pound to show you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Show it. I have heard both sums. I have not heard the jam.

speaker: james_burbage
text: The rope comes over a beam. The chair hangs on the rope. A god sits in the chair. Where the rope meets the block, a rope thick enough to hold a man will not take a neat turn. That is where it jams.

speaker: hired_men
text: I did not see a jam. I saw the book. The book says seven pounds and two shillings. The book does not say jam.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Then the book has not met a rope. I have met ropes. Ropes have opinions.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Put a man in the chair and the jam will introduce itself. I am only saying the chair is a chair until someone sits.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Not at this table. Let him finish the crust before anyone volunteers his neck.

speaker: james_burbage
text: A throne that comes down has to go up again, or your god is sitting among the groundlings for the rest of the play. That is the second cost, and nobody puts it in the seven pounds two shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it is a machine that must be struck as well as shown. I hear that.

speaker: agnes_tipping
text: The pork will be cold if the chair is still over the table when I come back for the plates.

speaker: hired_men
text: Eat, then. They have a new play and a chair. That is the whole of what I was given to say.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: And we have a dinner. I am beginning with the part I understand.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then begin. The chair can wait until the plate is clear.
